predecessors.note: Zwentibold's kingdom (895-900) fell to Louis the Child in 900; from 903 'Count Gebhard ... received the title of Duke of Lorraine' (Zwentibold page).

land.text: Lotharingia, the former Middle Francia (north): present-day Lorraine, Luxembourg, most of Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany west of the Rhine (Lotharingia page); the gazetteer region is the reading

predecessors.note: After 900 'Louis the Child, son of Arnulf, ruled over Lotharingia'.

successors.note: 'divided into two distinct duchies: Upper Lotharingia (southern half), and Lower Lotharingia (northern half)'. The duchy-of-lorraine dossier (Cliopatria row from 1431) reviews only 1431-1766; this is its earlier phase.
The northern half; no dossier yet (suggested slug duchy-of-lower-lorraine; Brabant, Limburg and the Rhineland west of the Rhine later).

rulers.name: Gebhard
rulers.title: Duke of Lorraine
rulers.note: A Conradine, first Lahngau count, then duke from 903. The pages give no end for Gebhard; a 'dux Lotharingiae' of 910 'may have been Gilbert' (Giselbert page).

rulers.name: Giselbert (Gilbert)
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: Son of Reginar; sided with Charles III in 911, invited Henry I in 923, switched to Rudolf in 924, swore fealty to Henry in 925, rebelled against Otto I in 939 and drowned fleeing on 2 October 939. The start year is the page's 910 reading; it is not firm.

rulers.name: Henry I, Duke of Bavaria
rulers.title: duke
rulers.note: 'Lorraine was then given to Henry I, Duke of Bavaria' after Andernach; the pages do not say how long he held it. The next dukes (Otto of Verdun 940-944, Conrad 944-954) are not on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Bruno
rulers.title: Archbishop of Cologne and duke
rulers.note: Otto 'deposed Conrad as duke of Lotharingia and appointed Bruno in his place' in 954; Bruno died on 11 October 965, after the 959 division.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's Middle Franks row ends 899; West Franks and East Franks / Kingdom of Germany shapes draw the land 903-959 as theirs). 'Since 903 it was organized as a duchy, which existed up to 959 or 965.' The pages give no frontier and no area; Alsace was inside the duchy in 923-925 (west-franks dossier) but the pages opened do not say so. fx-32 (F207): the gazetteer's Lotharingia region is whole Nordrhein-Westfalen and Rheinland-Pfalz, which put 177 cells of the East Frankish kingdom (Munster, Paderborn, Bielefeld, Dortmund, Essen, Wuppertal east of the Rhine; Worms, Speyer, Koblenz) inside this duchy for 903-958 and against kingdom-of-germany's 911-925 shapes. The Lotharingia page (opened 2026-11-01) puts the duchy in 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine', so the east bank cannot be Lotharingian; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany 922 shape (the East Frankish lands before Lotharingia joins in 925) is subtracted, which also takes the Worms-Speyer-Koblenz cells that Cliopatria draws as East Frankish. kingdom-of-germany's own shapes did not cover Lotharingia and are left as they are. [fx-32 review: the subtracted Kingdom of Germany 922 shape is cut to Germany. Uncut it also removed 18 cells in Drenthe, Overijssel and Gelderland (and 1 in France); the Lotharingia page (opened 2026-11-01) has the region include 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine, most of Belgium, and the Netherlands'.]

ledger.note: 959: The duchy is divided into Upper and Lower Lotharingia: 'divided into two distinct duchies: Upper Lotharingia (southern half), and Lower Lotharingia (northern half)', the date 959 or 965 being debated. The Bruno page: 'in 959 two local nobles, Godfrey and Frederick, were appointed as margraves of Lower Lotharingia and Upper Lotharingia respectively', recognised as dukes after Bruno's death in 965.

wars.name: Henry I's occupation of Lotharingia

zones.text: Lotharingia, the former Middle Francia (north): present-day Lorraine, Luxembourg, most of Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany west of the Rhine (Lotharingia page); the gazetteer region is the reading

wars.outcome: Giselbert and Archbishop Ruotger of Trier invited Henry I to invade in 923; Giselbert switched to King Rudolf in 924; in 925 Henry occupied Lotharingia and Giselbert swore fealty to him.
wars.note: The west-franks dossier books the 923-925 contest and the 925 loss to kingdom-of-germany.

wars.name: Giselbert's revolt against Otto I
wars.outcome: Giselbert rebelled against Otto I and changed allegiance to Louis IV of West Francia; he was defeated and made prisoner at Andernach and drowned crossing the Rhine on 2 October 939; Lorraine was then given to Henry I, Duke of Bavaria.

certainty.note: A stem duchy between two kingdoms whose frontier on the Meuse and Rhine is not given by any page opened; the duchy's overlord changed 911 (West Francia, Charles III), 923-925 (contest) and 925 (East Francia).

notes: Written for eu-07-x from four pages (Lotharingia, Zwentibold, Giselbert of Lorraine, Bruno the Great). This is the 903-959 phase of the Duchy of Lorraine whose later life (959-1766) belongs to duchy-of-lorraine (Cliopatria row 1431-1768, reviewed from 1431 only). A different slug is used because duchy-of-lorraine is another group's file; the colour agent should seed duchy-of-lotharingia in the same family as duchy-of-lorraine. Status problem: the duchy was a semi-autonomous stem duchy under changing overlords, but the east-franks (to 911), west-franks (911/11 'gain kingdom-of-germany ... Lotharingian duchy under Reginar'; 923-925 contest; 925 loss) and kingdom-of-germany dossiers book Lotharingia as direct royal land. If the duchy is drawn as its own state those holdings must be subtracted or turned into a vassal tint (vassal_start 911 by west-franks, 925 by kingdom-of-germany, with this slug as counterpart; vassal_end 959). Reginar's role is not on the pages opened: the Giselbert page gives him only as Giselbert's father; the 911 'sided with Charles III' sentence names no duke. Not on the pages (not drawn): Gebhard's death and the start of Giselbert's rule (the page's 910 'dux Lotharingiae' is only a possible reading), Otto of Verdun and Conrad the Red's terms, the 921 Treaty of Bonn, any frontier or capital (capitals left empty), Alsace's place in the duchy. Wikidata left null. The lower half has no dossier (suggested slug duchy-of-lower-lorraine). | fx-32 F207: keyframe, found and dissolve regions are now the gazetteer's Lotharingia less Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany 922 shape (177 East Frankish cells: Westphalia east of the Rhine, Worms-Speyer); the Lotharingia page puts the duchy in 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine'. Predecessor and successor lands still use the plain region (clipped to the state's cells on use).
